title: Localization criterion for a homotopically surjective map
statement: Use the universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]; the model-category conventions used below are stated explicitly in this node. Categories are complete and cocomplete, weak equivalences satisfy two-out-of-three and retract closure, and (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) and (trivial cofibrations, fibrations) are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. A weak factorization system consists of mutually characterized left and right diagonal-lifting classes and factorizations of all arrows; trivial means also a weak equivalence. Cofibrant and fibrant mean that the initial and terminal maps, respectively, are cofibrations and fibrations. A cofibrant replacement is a trivial fibration $QX\to X$ with $QX$ cofibrant; a fibrant replacement is a trivial cofibration $X\to TX$ with $TX$ fibrant. Combinatorial means locally presentable with small generating sets $I,J$ whose right lifting classes are the trivial fibrations and fibrations, respectively. Locally presentable means cocomplete and generated, for some regular $\kappa$, under $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve these colimits. A Quillen adjunction is an ordinary adjunction whose left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. It is a Quillen equivalence when, for each cofibrant source object $A$ and fibrant target object $Y$, a map $LA\to Y$ is a weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $A\to RY$ is a weak equivalence. Left proper means that pushout of a weak equivalence along a cofibration is a weak equivalence. Write $\mathsf{sSet}$ for the simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] with the Kan model structure: cofibrations are monomorphisms; fibrations have the right lifting property against all horns $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ ($n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$), where $\Delta^n$ is the representable simplex and $\Lambda_i^n$ is the union of its faces other than the $i$th; weak equivalences induce a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on all homotopy groups of geometric realizations. A simplicial model category is enriched, tensored and cotensored over $\mathsf{sSet}$, with the induced map of mapping simplicial sets for a cofibration and a fibration a Kan fibration, trivial if either arrow is trivial. For a simplicial model category $\mathcal A$, write $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}^h(A,Z)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}(QA,TZ)$ for derived mapping spaces, computed with cofibrant and fibrant replacements in its original structure; equivalence of spaces means weak homotopy equivalence of these Kan complexes. For a set $S$ of arrows of $\mathcal A$, an object $Z$ is $S$-local if $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal A}^h(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $(A\to B)\in S$. A left Bousfield localization $L_S\mathcal A$ is a model structure on the same category with the same cofibrations and with weak equivalences the maps inducing equivalences of these mapping spaces into every fibrant $S$-local object. Let $L:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:R$ be a Quillen adjunction between combinatorial model categories, with $\mathcal M$ left proper and simplicial. Suppose that, for every fibrant $X$ in $\mathcal N$ and every cofibrant replacement $q:QRX\to RX$, the composite $LQRX\xrightarrow{Lq}LRX\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_X}X$ is a weak equivalence (homotopical surjectivity). Choose a functorial cofibrant-replacement functor $Q$ in $\mathcal M$. Then there is a small set $S$ of arrows of $\mathcal M$ such that $LQ(s)$ is a weak equivalence for each $s\in S$, and the same adjoint functors induce a Quillen equivalence $L_S\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N$.

source.place: Definition 3.1 and Proposition 3.2, printed pp. 181-182, specialized to a simplicial source (no simpliciality assumption on the target). Homotopy function complexes then use the simplicial replacement formula.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-dugger-cardinal-choice] to the given combinatorial Quillen adjunction. Choose its regular $\lambda$, small full subcategory $\mathcal M_\lambda$, functorial cofibrant replacement $Q_0\to\mathrm{id}$ in $\mathcal M$, and fibrant replacement $\mathrm{id}\to T$ in $\mathcal N$. These are auxiliary choices; the functor $Q$ in the conclusion need not preserve filtered colimits. For each $A\in\mathcal M_\lambda$ put $C_A=Q_0A$, $Y_A=TL C_A$, and let $s_A:C_A\to RY_A$ be adjoint to the fibrant replacement $r_A:LC_A\to Y_A$. The arrows $s_A$ form a small set $S$ because they are indexed by the objects of the small category $\mathcal M_\lambda$. They also give the components of the natural transformation $s_X:Q_0X\to RTLQ_0X$ defined by the same adjunction formula for every $X$.

source.place: Proposition 3.2 proof, conditions (1)-(5) and definition of S, printed pp. 181-182.

proof.text: Use the derived adjunction of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], and pass to its homotopy categories (ordinary localizations, by the localization universal property). Homotopical surjectivity says its counit $\overline\varepsilon_{Y_A}:\mathbf LL\mathbf RR(Y_A)\to Y_A$ is invertible. The adjunction formula for $s_A$ gives $\overline\varepsilon_{Y_A}\circ\mathbf LL(s_A)=[r_A]$, under the replacement identifications, and $r_A$ is a weak equivalence. Thus $\mathbf LL(s_A)$ is invertible. The replacement formula for the derived functor and [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences], applied in $\mathcal N$, imply that $LQ(s_A)$ is a weak equivalence for the functor $Q$ fixed in the statement, as well as for $Q_0$. This proves the required image condition without assuming $\mathcal N$ simplicial or that $Q$ is accessible.

source.place: Definition 3.1 and Proposition 3.2 proof, why Lcof inverts S, printed pp. 181-182.

proof.text: For each $s_A:C_A\to RY_A$, factor it in the original model structure as a cofibration $i_A:C_A\to B_A$ followed by a trivial fibration $p_A:B_A\to RY_A$. Both $C_A$ and $B_A$ are cofibrant. The square from $i_A$ to $s_A$ has vertical maps $1_{C_A}$ and $p_A$, which are weak equivalences. The natural derived mapping-space comparison in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] therefore identifies the locality tests for the small set $S$ with those for the small set $I=\{i_A\}$. For cofibrant endpoints and fibrant test objects, the enriched mapping sets represent these same derived spaces. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-bousfield-model-structure] to $I$. Its hypotheses hold because $\mathcal M$ is left proper, combinatorial and simplicial and $I$ consists of cofibrations between cofibrant objects. The resulting $L_I\mathcal M$ has exactly the $S$-local weak equivalences and the original cofibrations; denote it $L_S\mathcal M$. In particular every $s_A$ is a weak equivalence there by its defining locality test.

source.place: Proposition 3.2 proof, formation of M/S; cofibrant-cofibration normalization makes explicit the hypotheses of the cited Bousfield existence node, printed p. 182.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-bousfield-quillen-descent] to $L\dashv R$, the small set $S$, the model structure of Step 3 and the image condition of Step 2. It supplies the Quillen adjunction $L:L_S\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:R$. Since a model structure's trivial fibrations are precisely the right lifting class of its cofibrations, unchanged cofibrations mean unchanged trivial fibrations and cofibrant objects. Consequently every $Q_0X\to X$ is also a cofibrant replacement in $L_S\mathcal M$. For fibrant $Y\in\mathcal N$ its derived counit is still represented by $LQ_0RY\to Y$, which is a weak equivalence by the original homotopical-surjectivity assumption and the derived replacement formula. Thus the descended adjunction remains homotopically surjective.

source.place: Proposition 3.2 proof, descent and continued homotopical surjectivity, printed p. 182; descent is Hirschhorn Proposition 3.3.18(1).

proof.text: Here is the filtered-colimit inheritance argument suppressed at the end of Dugger's proof. Fix a small $\lambda$-filtered category $J$ and a diagram map $f:D\to E$ whose components are weak equivalences in $L_S\mathcal M$. By [lem-coef-model-colimit-localization-comparison], both $\mathcal M^J$ and $(L_S\mathcal M)^J$ have projective model structures. Their projective cofibrations agree: their trivial fibrations are the same objectwise trivial fibrations, since the base cofibrations agree. Take functorial projective cofibrant replacements $PD\to D$ and $PE\to E$ in the original projective structure. They are also cofibrant replacements in the localized projective structure, and two-out-of-three makes $P(f)$ a weak equivalence there. The colimit-constant-diagram adjunction is Quillen for the localized projective structure: its right adjoint preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations because these are objectwise. Thus the weak-equivalence preservation clause of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] makes $\operatorname{colim}P(f)$ a localized weak equivalence. Meanwhile the comparison maps $\operatorname{colim}PD\to\operatorname{colim}D$ and $\operatorname{colim}PE\to\operatorname{colim}E$ are original weak equivalences by the $\lambda$-filtered weak-equivalence closure in [lem-coef-dugger-cardinal-choice], since the replacement maps are objectwise original weak equivalences. Original weak equivalences are local weak equivalences by Step 3's mapping-space test. Two-out-of-three now proves that $\operatorname{colim}f$ is a localized weak equivalence. The category $J$ is explicitly small; no existence theorem for large projective diagram categories is invoked.

source.place: Proposition 3.2 proof, final sentence on inheritance of filtered-colimit preservation by localization, printed p. 182; expanded projective-replacement argument.

proof.text: For any $X\in\mathcal M$, choose a small $\lambda$-filtered diagram $A:J\to\mathcal M_\lambda$ with colimit $X$, using [lem-coef-dugger-cardinal-choice]. The functors $Q_0,T,R$ preserve these colimits by that node, and $L$ preserves all colimits because it is a left adjoint. Hence the source and target of $s_X:Q_0X\to RTLQ_0X$ identify with the corresponding colimits of the sources and targets of the $s_{A_j}$. Naturality of the unit and of the replacement maps makes these identifications identify the arrow itself: on each colimit injection its composite is $s_{A_j}$ followed by the target injection, which determines a map out of the colimit. Each $s_{A_j}$ is a localized weak equivalence by Step 3, so Step 5 makes $s_X$ a localized weak equivalence. By the replacement formula of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] and the weak equivalence $Q_0X\to X$, this is exactly invertibility of the derived unit of the descended adjunction for every object.

source.place: Proposition 3.2 proof, filtered-colimit computation of the derived unit, printed p. 182.

proof.text: The descended derived adjunction has invertible unit by Step 6 and invertible counit by Step 4. For completeness, the Quillen-equivalence test follows directly: for a cofibrant $A$ and fibrant $Y$, if $f:LA\to Y$ has adjoint $g:A\to RY$, the derived adjunction formulas give $[g]=\mathbf RR([f])\circ\overline\eta_A$ and $[f]=\overline\varepsilon_Y\circ\mathbf LL([g])$. Thus either arrow being invertible implies the other is invertible, because both comparison transformations are invertible. Apply [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] in $\mathcal N$ and $L_S\mathcal M$ to replace invertibility with weak equivalence. Thus, for each cofibrant $A$ and fibrant $Y$, the map $f:LA\to Y$ is a weak equivalence exactly when its adjoint $g:A\to RY$ is a weak equivalence. Together with Step 2 it proves both conclusions.

source.place: Definition 3.1 and Proposition 3.2 proof, final Quillen-equivalence verification, printed pp. 181-182.
